name: Nucleus Genomics (mynucleus.com)
category: genetics — consumer whole-genome sequencing (30x WGS) pivoting to reproductive/fertility genetics (preconception couple screening + IVF embryo selection)
country: USA (NYC HQ). Ships kits to US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Italy, France, Czech Republic, India, UAE, New Zealand. IVF+ clinic network extends to India (160+ Indira Fertility clinics), Jordan, Mexico; expanded to Saudi Arabia. Not present in Brazil.
stage: startup — ~$32M total funding, Series A Jan 2025 ($14M, Founders Fund); strategic pivot 2024-2026 from consumer health WGS toward high-ticket fertility/embryo selection ('Have Your Best Baby' campaign, Nov 2025)
pricing_model: Kit + mandatory recurring membership. Current US pricing: Nucleus Health $499 one-time (HSA/FSA eligible; was ~$400 at Jan 2025 per TechCrunch) + per-person/year membership required to access results — membership price not disclosed on any static page, even archived snapshots [uncertain]. Nucleus Preview: two kits + membership (price JS-injected, unresolved [uncertain]). Nucleus Embryo: $9,999 package (both-parent Preview + analysis of up to 20 embryos + genetic counselor session). Nucleus IVF+: 'as little as $9,999/month for four months' (~$40k, varies by clinic/location). Genetic counseling via SteadyMD: $99/hour, not included in membership (included with Embryo; unlimited with IVF+).
target_user: Originally proactive-health consumers/biohackers; now primarily affluent couples planning pregnancy and IVF patients; secondary channels: employers (benefits), IVF clinics (B2B2C), creators/influencers (free/discounted kits)
scale_metrics: Funding $32M total: $3.5M seed (Dec 2021), $14M Series A (Jan 2025) — Founders Fund, Seven Seven Six (Alexis Ohanian), Peter Thiel, Balaji Srinivasan, Samsung Next, Asylum Ventures, One Eight Capital, Achal Upadhyaya. Valuation undisclosed. User counts undisclosed; company claims 'thousands of patients served' and 165+ IVF clinic partners. Acquired Irish AI health-data platform Cambrean (early 2025). Durability signal: pivot from $499 consumer WGS (crowded, 23andMe-bankruptcy vacuum) to $9,999-$40k fertility bundles = margin migration to the action loop; but heavy reputational drag (scientific controversy, Genomic Prediction federal lawsuit) — a durable threat in the genetics niche, not in lab-panel interpretation.
core_features: Nucleus Health: 30x whole-genome sequencing from at-home cheek swab; risk reports for 2,000+ conditions and traits (hereditary cancers incl. HBOC/Lynch-type, heart disease, coronary artery disease, hypertension, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, T1/T2 diabetes, celiac, ADHD/anxiety/depression/OCD, male-pattern baldness); pharmacogenomics not prominently marketed on the current site [uncertain]
Raw DNA sovereignty: download whole genome as VCF, CRAM, SV, CNV, FASTQ + formats for Promethease/GEDmatch upload
Nucleus Preview: preconception test for couples — both partners sequenced, simulates what a future child could inherit (2,000+ conditions incl. CF/SMA, plus traits eye color/height/IQ)

Nucleus Embryo: IVF embryo analysis — rare disease (PGT-M add-on), polygenic long-term risks (cancers, T1D/T2D, heart, psychiatric), traits (height, eye/hair color, IQ) across up to 20 embryos; embryo ranking for selection
Nucleus IVF+: full concierge IVF journey — clinic matching, care coordination, donor guidance, unlimited genetic counseling, Preview + Embryo included
Nucleus AI: personalized health-tips layer combining DNA + lifestyle factors
Membership: results update over time as models improve ('weather forecast' framing — new diseases/traits added)
Genetic counseling via partner SteadyMD ($99/h; included with Embryo/IVF+)
signature_differentiator: Only consumer platform spanning the full 'generational health' stack: clinical-grade 30x whole-genome sequencing of both parents ($499 entry, ~100% of DNA vs 23andMe's <0.1% array) + probabilistic simulation of a future child (Preview) + polygenic embryo ranking for IVF selection incl. IQ/height/disease risk (Embryo, $9,999) + bundled concierge IVF care (IVF+). The couple-to-embryo continuity on one genome platform is the signature nobody else offers.
lab_data_handling: Does NOT handle lab exams/blood panels at all — zero PDF upload, no lab integrations, no biomarker interpretation. Own pipeline: at-home cheek swab → prepaid mail → third-party CLIA-certified/CAP-accredited labs (Illumina sequencing, 30x coverage) → results in 4-6 weeks. Genome is static: no retest cadence, no annual blood, no hardware/CGM/wearable — instead re-analysis updates as models improve. Embryo data ingested offline from existing PGT labs. Cambrean acquisition (Irish AI health-data platform, early 2025) hints at future biomarker aggregation but nothing shipped publicly [uncertain].
family_dependents_depth: Deepest-in-market for the FUTURE family: couple carrier + expanded screening (HBOC, Lynch 50%-inheritance explicitly marketed), future-child inheritance simulation, donor support (donor Preview with identity privacy), embryo-level hereditary risk ranking before implantation. But nothing for EXISTING families: no dependent profiles, no pediatric ranges, no caregiver mode, no longitudinal family health record. Family = next-generation planning, not household management.
doctor_sharing: Lightweight: Health results framed as a 'starting point for conversations with your doctor' (patient-initiated, no structured brief). Embryo/IVF+ results are shared with the IVF care team including the physician by default, with Nucleus genetic counselors working alongside the clinic. No physician portal, no SOAP/consult-brief product, no clinical summary export beyond standard reports.
action_loop_monetization: Ladder monetization after first result: annual membership renewal (access to updated/new reports — effectively a paywall on your own results), $99/h counseling upsell, Health → Preview → Embryo ($9,999) → IVF+ (~$40k) upgrade path, PGT-M add-ons, employer benefits channel, clinic B2B2C channel, 'Nucleus Cares' access program. 'Nucleus AI' personalized tips = the lifestyle action loop. No supplements, no prescriptions, no telemedicine marketplace. The margin lives in fertility bundles, not the $499 WGS.
ai_approach: Proprietary polygenic risk score (PRS) engine — whitepaper 'Nucleus Origin' describes SBayesRC-style models trained on UK Biobank; marketed as 'the most predictive genetic models ever built'. 'Nucleus AI' adds an LLM-style personalized health-tips layer. Sequencing outsourced to third-party CLIA/CAP labs. Human-in-the-loop = SteadyMD genetic counselors, not clinical review of results. Credibility contested: independent critique (Nov 2025) alleges the Origin whitepaper extensively copies competitor Herasight's preprint, contains train/validation overlap, wrong ICD mappings (ICD9 714 rheumatoid-arthritis code used for prostate cancer), and that many marketed scores derive from only 6-50 variants recycled from open-source repositories.
data_inputs: DNA only today: 30x WGS cheek swab (single genome), couple pairing (two genomes) for Preview, embryo PGT data for Embryo. Marketing claims Health combines 'DNA with lifestyle factors' for personalized insights, but no structured lifestyle/wearable/lab inputs are documented [uncertain]. No questionnaire-based intake documented.
data_interoperability: Export-strong, import-blind. OUT: whole-genome download (VCF, CRAM, SV, CNV, FASTQ), Promethease/GEDmatch-ready formats, Origin License Agreement for data licensing, HIPAA/SOC 2 posture. IN: nothing — no FHIR, no Apple Health Records, no Health Connect, no PDF/lab upload, no LIS/API integration (embryo data flows via offline clinic coordination). Ingestion moat absent; exhaustion moat (raw genome sovereignty) real.
platform: Web only: Framer marketing site + web app reports dashboard ('Nucleus account'). No native iOS or Android app found in App Store / Google Play searches (Aug 2026), despite 'app' language in marketing [uncertain — a native app may exist unlisted or be web-wrapped].
onboarding: DTC flow: shop online → kit arrives 6-10 business days → two cheek swabs at home → prepaid return (5-7 days transit) → results ~4-5 weeks after lab confirms receipt (4-6 weeks total). Time-to-value 5-7 weeks from order. Fertility paths get white-glove: 2-minute eligibility quiz + concierge team (concierge@mynucleus.com) coordinates directly with the IVF clinic; embryo analysis ready 1-2 weeks after embryo data received.
data_visualization: Web dashboard reports, self-described 'clear, easy-to-understand'. Core literacy device: dichotomy between definitive single-gene results (variant present/absent) and probabilistic polygenic likelihood (risk, not guarantee) — explicitly taught in the FAQ. Embryo product shows side-by-side comparison across up to 20 embryos. Results are versioned: they change as models improve ('earlier results weren't wrong, just less refined' — weather-forecast metaphor). No longitudinal biomarker trend charts (genome is static).
engagement_channel: Membership as retention spine: pay the annual fee or lose access to your own results + future updates — a built-in renewal mechanic (also the most criticized UX decision). Email newsletter ('join the movement'), concierge white-glove support, 'Nucleus Stories' testimonial content, creator/influencer seeding. No streaks, no community, no WhatsApp, no push channel. Fundamentally a transactional test with a subscription paywall, not a habit product.
clinical_validation_trust: CLAIMS: >99.9% accuracy for WGS (a sequencing-level claim — defensible); 'validated, peer-reviewed research'; 'most predictive genetic models ever built'; 'thousands of patients'. EVIDENCE BASE: weak and contested — no independent peer-reviewed validation of their PRS performance; the Origin whitepaper is accused of plagiarizing Herasight's preprint (near-identical SBayesRC methodology and wording) and contains basic errors (train/validation overlap, ICD9 714 used for prostate cancer, duplicate UKB codes, scores allegedly built from 6-50 variants). Named scientific critics: Sasha Gusev (Harvard, 'not yet clinically actionable'), Eric Turkheimer ('new eugenics company'), Arthur Caplan & James Tabery (Scientific American, Theranos comparison), Ruxandra Teslo ('non-rigorous'). NHGRI position cited against PRS actionability. Testimonials alleged fabricated (stock photos, chronologically impossible claims, AI faces). Federal lawsuit from former partner Genomic Prediction alleging co-founder Nathan Treff stole proprietary embryo methods and deleted data before resigning. Pricing transparency: good (clear $499/$9,999 pricing). Billing transparency: membership required to see own results = recurring-charge criticism. No clinical advisory board prominently published.
regulatory_posture: US LDT (laboratory-developed test) posture: CLIA-certified, CAP-accredited lab network; HIPAA-compliant; SOC 2 Type II. No FDA authorization/clearance claimed anywhere on site, and no public FDA enforcement action found [uncertain]; operates in the post-FDA-LDT-crackdown gray zone. ToS reportedly contains contradictory statements about physician review of results; prohibits processing samples from New York residents while being NYC-based and advertising in NY — classic lab-network workaround. International: ships to 12+ countries; embryo trait-selection services restricted in the UK and India, where selecting embryos on certain characteristics is illegal. Disclaimers: probabilistic framing ('more information, not instructions'; 'likelihood, not guarantees'), no diagnosis claims, genetic-counselor availability emphasized. LGPD/ANVISA: not applicable — no Brazil presence. For the Dr. Exame benchmark: their compliance = CLIA/CAP + probabilistic disclaimers with weak physician-review transparency — Dr. Exame's explicit non-diagnosis guardrails + physician-sharing flow would exceed their posture in a BR context.
gaps_opportunities: WHAT THEY DON'T DO (Dr. Exame openings): no lab-exam/blood-panel interpretation whatsoever (genome ≠ current metabolic reality — TSH, glucose, lipids invisible to them); no longitudinal biomarker trends; no existing-family dependents/caregiver/pediatric layer; no doctor-facing brief or SOAP; no conversational/WhatsApp channel; no ingestion of any external health data (export-only); no Brazil/LatAm presence and no Portuguese (only EN/ES); clinicians actively distrust the brand (wedge for evidence-based positioning). WHAT WORKS (inspiration, not copy): the 'generational health' narrative — genome as a family asset passed to children; results-that-update-over-time membership mechanic (reframe recurring value as 'your report gets smarter' — but never paywall access to already-delivered results); raw-data sovereignty (VCF/FASTQ download builds trust); clean probabilistic-vs-definitive literacy framing in the FAQ; high-ticket bundled care with concierge (IVF+) proving willingness to pay $9,999-$40k when stakes are family-level; couple/preconception category creation (900+ conditions couple compatibility).
relevance: Medium. Validates the thesis that the genetic layer is a data class panel-apps lack (their $32M raised + pivot proves consumer willingness to pay for genome + family risk), and their family-planning depth is the closest thing to Dr. Exame's family pillar. But direct overlap with Dr. Exame is low: no lab interpretation, no longitudinal monitoring, no Brazil presence, heavy scientific-controversy baggage. Watch as: (a) proof the 'genetic layer' premium exists, (b) a potential future partner/white-label for WGS ingestion, (c) a cautionary tale on PRS overclaiming and testimonial authenticity.
